speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for National Development with the recent announcements of the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme, Home Improvement Programme II and relaxation of CPF rules for purchase of older flats, to what extent do these measures address the concerns on the lease decay issue and how do the measures support long-term urban planning in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether he can provide more information about the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS); (b) what is the projected timeframe for its implementation; (c) which are the precincts that will be eligible; and (d) how will the compensation package be computed.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Government's offer to buy back HDB flats older than 70 years extends to all flats or only selected ones; (b) what will be the selection criteria for the eligible VERS precincts; and (c) what options will residents have if they fail to get VERS for their flat.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what are the factors considered in the planning phase for the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme; and (b) whether the private developers will have a role in the redevelopment programme and, if so, can more details be shared.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Government is committed to strengthening our institution of public housing and home ownership, so that it continues to bring tangible benefits to current and future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is why at the recent National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong highlighted the Ministry of National Development's (MND's) plans to systematically upgrade older HDB flats through the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) and HIP II, and to progressively renew and rebuild older HDB towns through the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Various Members have asked about the details of VERS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of our older housing estates were built up in a hurry to meet the housing needs of Singaporeans at that time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: By spreading out the redevelopment of these towns over a span of 20 to 30 years through VERS, we can avoid having to rebuild entire towns in a similar hurry, which would be highly disruptive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This large-scale redevelopment effort is a good opportunity not only to rebuild some of our older precincts, but also to introduce new and exciting concepts of living in our newer towns into our older towns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To achieve this, we will need to carefully study how to select the precincts and stage the redevelopment, precinct by precinct, town by town.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have already explained the broad concept of VERS and how it is different from the Selective En Bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: SERS is limited to precincts where there is high development value to be unlocked.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because of the value unlocked, we share this value with residents through generous compensation, and the acquisition can be made compulsory.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have outlined the broad concept of VERS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there are still many details to work out, and we will need time to do so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This includes the extent of coverage of VERS and how the compensation will be computed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In particular, we will ensure that we implement VERS in a fiscally sustainable way, so that it does not become a burden for the next generation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For residents who do not get VERS for their flat, or who do not poll in favour of VERS, they will continue to live in their flats which would have benefited from two rounds of upgrading.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It could be a new flat from HDB for those who are eligible; a resale flat on a shorter lease; or a 2-room flexi flat for retirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will have various options to cater to diverse needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Miss Cheryl Chan has asked whether private developers will have a role in the redevelopment programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, in the case of SERS today, we already, from time to time, inject some private development in the redevelopment process.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, for VERS, going forward, I will not rule out the possibility of having private developers being involved, and we will study her suggestion carefully.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our aim is to redevelop public housing estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will ensure that any redevelopment is done in a way that preserves the character of our HDB towns and supports HDB's mission to provide affordable and quality homes for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Whether they come to pass depends on our external, economic and financial situation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But this Government has a track record of delivering on our commitments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to work with all Singaporeans to translate our plans into reality and build a better Singapore for the future.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The first is on the guidelines for selecting the precincts for VERS.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Is it purely based on age or are there other factors?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The second question is: what percentage of votes will be considered successful during the polling in VERS, in order to qualify for it?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am afraid these are details that we will have to study and I do not have a reply today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think it would be premature to talk about such details now, because we are, indeed, going through a very thorough study of how to go about implementing VERS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These issues will be incorporated into our study.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I know it is going to be 20 years more before you are going to share what VERS is.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But can the Minister share, in terms of timeline, how soon will the residents who would potentially be in the precinct be informed of the potential of their precincts being included in the VERS selection?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, I will ask a question in reverse of the hon Member Mr Saktiandi's.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How long would this study take and when can we expect that the Ministry will come back to the House to share more details once the study is concluded?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we have been looking at this issue for quite some time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have already indicated the broad roadmap, if you will, for how we think about housing redevelopment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: From now, going forward, there are quite a number of major items that have to be put in place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are talking about the next batch of flats that are built between 1987 and 1997.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is a major programme, assuming we have the budget for it, to roll out HIP II.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are details that will have to be looked at.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we put all these in place, it is really quite a major series of initiatives and programmes that will have to be implemented.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will do it step by step, systematically.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For SERS, we have already selected many of the sites with high development potential.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For SERS, there are a few more sites.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we will continue to implement SERS in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not intend to hold back the SERS programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On financial sustainability, that is a very important point that Dr Lily Neo has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as I said earlier, we are committed to ensuring that even as we have laid out the broad roadmap for public housing going forward, we are committed to ensuring that whatever we do, it is done in a way that it is sustainable over the long term.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Taking reference from en bloc sales in private estates, how would the Government prevent the high possibility of the VERS exercise becoming very acrimonious?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Also, how does the Government then intend to protect the rights of the minority who might object to the exercise, just like in the private sector?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Government must have thought through before announcing VERS.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What lessons can be drawn from private en bloc exercises and what could be prevented to make sure that these problems do not occur or recur similarly in the public housing exercise?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They worry that the process of voting for VERS can end up with an acrimonious situation amongst neighbours.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I would say this process of getting votes for upgrading is not new.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB has done it before, of course, under more limited upgrading programmes like lift upgrading and HIP.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister, just to clarify, were you planning to take Question No 5 together with the first four?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will take Question Nos 5 and 6 later.
